title: Secretome analysis of primary CLL cells
projectDescription: Secretome analysis of primary CLL cells co-cultured in serum-free IMDM medium with either EL08 stroma cells or YK6 follicular dendritic cells overexpressing CD40L and interleukin 21 (“FDC CD40L IL21”).
sampleProcessingProtocol: Supernatants were collected after 6 hours, centrifuged, filtered and processed by acetone precipitation before being analyzed by high-sensitivity mass-spectrometry-based proteomics. Secretomes were denaturated, reduced, and alkylated with 1% SDC, 10 mM TCEP, 40 mM CA), and 150 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.5, for 10 min at 95 °C and 1,000 rpm. Proteins were digested overnight under gentle agitation (700 rpm) at 37 °C with trypsin with an enzyme:substrate ratio of 1:50. SDC was precipitated by acidification to 5% of formic acid. Prior to mass-spectrometry analysis, samples were desalted by the AssayMAP Bravo Platform using 5 μL RP-S cartridges and the standard peptide cleanup v3.0 protocol.
dataProcessingProtocol: LC-MS/MS measurements were performed using a Vanquish Neo UHPLC coupled to the Orbitrap Exploris 480 mass spectrometer. Peptides were delivered to a trap column (75 μm i.d. × 5 cm, packed in-house with 5 μm of Reprosil C18 beads) using 0.1% formic acid at a flow rate of  5 μL/min. Subsequently, peptides were transferred to an analytical column (75 μm i.d. × 43 cm, packed in-house with 1.9 μm Reprosil C18 beads) at a flow rate of 300 nL/min and chromatographically separated using a 171 min linear gradient of solvent B (0.1% formic acid, 3% DMSO in ACN) and solvent A (0.1% formic acid, 3% DMSO in water). The total measurement time for each sample was 180 min. DIA was performed with one full MS scan followed by 46 MS/MS covering precursor masses from 360 m/z to 1,300 m/z with variable isolation windows. The full MS events were recorded with an AGC of 300%, a maxIT of 50 ms and a resolution of 120,000. MS/MS spectra were acquired with an NCE of 30% using an AGC of 3,000%, a maxIT of 54 ms, and a resolution of 30,000. DIA-NN 1.8.1 was used to analyze DIA data against an in-silico-generated library from the UniProtKB Human database (UP000005640, containing canonical and isoform sequences, downloaded on 10/2023). The default settings were kept, except the charge state was set to 2 to 4, and the precursor’s m/z range was restricted from 360 to 1,300 m/z. Identifications were filtered for a maximum of 1% FDR at precursor and global protein levels.
